meta.title: Bit-banged SPI and its maximum clock rate
meta.tools: C firmware (software SPI, modes 0 and 3) with a per-instruction cycle-cost model, logic-analyser decode in Python
meta.summary: Implement SPI in software on GPIO pins, count the CPU cycles per bit to predict the maximum SCLK, and decode the generated waveform to verify mode, bit order and data.
meta.problem: When a microcontroller lacks a free SPI peripheral, you toggle pins yourself. How fast can that go, and does the timing still meet the protocol?
meta.theory:
Per bit: set MOSI (≈ 3 cycles for read-modify-write), SCLK high (2), read MISO (2), SCLK low (2), shift/loop (≈ 5) → ~14 cycles at 16 MHz
= 0.875 µs/bit → ≈ 1.14 MHz max SCLK, with an asymmetric duty cycle (high for 4 of 14 cycles).
meta.method:
Cycle-cost model inside the simulated HAL (cycles advance simulated time at 16 MHz). 64 bytes sent in modes 0 and 3; Python decodes SCLK/MOSI and measures
the period and duty; data compared with the sent bytes.

rows.quantity: Maximum SCLK (16 MHz / 14 cycles per bit)
